elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New Article XIII-A says only "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee"; there is no "defend" or "hold harmless" obligation, and no reference to Licensee's affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A runs in favour of "Licensee" only; affiliates are covered only in the Licensee-side indemnity in Article XII ("Licensor or any of its affiliates").

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee against any third-party claim alleging that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right"; Licensed Technology is the defined licensed deliverable (Licensed Know-How and Licensed Software).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A is limited to IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no breach-of-law prong was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer Data prong appears in Article XIII-A.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence or wilful misconduct prong in Article XIII-A; Article XIII's blanket Licensor exclusions remain otherwise intact.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic was added; Article XIII-A contains only the grant, exclusions, remedies and cap.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No control-of-defence sentence in Article XIII-A.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation in Article XIII-A.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Article XII is retained unchanged and still covers "Licensee's exercise of any license or other rights", "the conduct of Licensee's business" and any breach of the Agreement — far broader than Customer-provided content and breach of law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A: "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee against any third-party claim alleging that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right"; the retained Article XIII infringement bar is expressly made "SUBJECT TO ARTICLE XIII-A", so no contradiction survives.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Carve-out (i): "modifications to the Licensed Technology made by Licensee".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Carve-out (ii): "combination of the Licensed Technology with items not supplied by Licensor".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall, at its option, procure the right for Licensee to continue using, modify, or replace the affected Licensed Technology".

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "if none of those remedies is reasonably available, shall refund the fees paid for the affected Licensed Technology".

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "Licensor's total liability for its indemnification obligations under this Article XIII-A shall not exceed three (3) times the fees paid by Licensee to Licensor under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 3x annualised-fee super-cap, and Article XIII(b)'s 0.5x cap is expressly made subject to it.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred element; noted only because the inserted cap in Article XIII-A also governs the new indemnity.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the inserted Article XIII-A supplies a Licensor IP indemnity, the three customary Licensee-side exclusions, procure/modify/replace remedies, a fees refund fallback, and an express 3x trailing-12-month fees super-cap.

Preferred level is not reached and is not claimed: no duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, no breach-of-law/data-breach/gross-negligence prongs, no notice/control/cooperation procedure, and Article XII's broad Licensee indemnity is untouched.

Minimality holds: a concise insertion for a missing clause plus two surgical "SUBJECT TO ARTICLE XIII-A" conforming edits that are strictly necessary to stop the retained Article XIII infringement bar and 0.5x cap from nullifying the new indemnity. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added, and no favourable existing wording was deleted.

Intent preserved: Article XII, the Article XIII consequential-damages exclusion and the general 0.5x cap all survive for non-indemnity matters; the new Article XIII-A cross-reference is defined and creates no dangling term.

Actionable improvement (not a failure at fallback): the "SUBJECT TO ARTICLE XIII-A" qualifier was placed only ahead of the infringement sentence and Article XIII(b). Consider extending it to the opening consequential/indirect damages exclusion in Article XIII(a) so Licensor cannot argue that indemnified third-party sums are excluded categories of loss.

Note: paragraph (c) ("THIS SECTION IS A MATERIAL INDUCEMENT...") appears in the rendered text but not in the cited original excerpt; it reads as pre-existing Licensor-favourable context rather than a drafter addition, and is not scored against minimality. Confirm it was not introduced by the edit.
